evidence.detail: Checkout HEAD and supplied target both resolve to 2495c32df08ee11a563122bde4a5fca6fe93fae1; supplied base resolves to 98a20bc479b55b1cdab5e8958ed3630bff0e044a. The worktree was clean.
evidence.reference: git status --short; git rev-parse HEAD; git rev-parse 98a20bc479b55b1cdab5e8958ed3630bff0e044a; git rev-parse 2495c32df08ee11a563122bde4a5fca6fe93fae1

evidence.detail: The exact base-to-target diff adds graph.py and tests/test_graph.py and changes server.py, tests/test_server.py, the issue record, handoff, and current status.
Independent tests ran 42 tests but exited 1: 32 completed and all 10 server integration tests errored because the read-only sandbox prohibited binding 127.0.0.1.
Independent compilation exited 1 because py_compile could not create __pycache__ in the read-only checkout.
Governance validation exited 1 because no writable temporary directory was available to its launcher smoke tests.
The handoff claims compile exit 0, 42 passing tests, and governance success from author-run out-of-band checks, but this review cannot independently verify complete successful execution.
No live tenant fetch was attempted because it is a separately protected action and is explicitly not an issue-completion prerequisite.

evidence: Expected: every bearer-authenticated request must remain restricted to Microsoft Graph, as required by the issue stop condition and security boundary.

Observed: fetch_policies assigns an arbitrary string from @odata.nextLink directly to url and sends the Authorization header through the injected/default transport on the next iteration. urllib_graph_transport performs no scheme or hostname validation, despite its comment claiming only Microsoft Graph URLs reach it.
A response containing an https://attacker.example next link would therefore receive the tenant access token. Redirect handling is also not explicitly constrained or validated.
The existing paging test accepts a next-link URL but does not test rejection of non-Graph hosts or redirects.
findings.remediation: Validate every initial, paged, and redirected destination before attaching credentials: require HTTPS and the exact approved Microsoft Graph hostname (and an appropriate path policy). Disable redirects or implement a redirect handler that reapplies the same validation. Return a stable GraphError for rejected destinations and add tests proving arbitrary hosts, userinfo/hostname tricks, non-HTTPS URLs, and redirects cannot receive the bearer token.
findings.title: Unvalidated next links can exfiltrate the bearer token
findings.verification: Use a recording transport/HTTP test double with malicious next links and redirects; verify no request is made and no Authorization header leaves the approved Graph origin. Then rerun compilation and the full test suite.

evidence: Expected: the prerequisite contract must define the optional local, user-supplied break-glass object-ID input and specify that the corresponding analyzer rule is not evaluable when it is absent.

Observed: the handoff's recorded contract lists only normalized policy fields. It contains no shape, validation/sanitization rules, supply mechanism, or absent-input behavior for the required break-glass input.
ISSUE-0004 is expressly required to bind its rules to this contract, so leaving this portion unspecified carries the planning ambiguity forward.
findings.remediation: Extend the durable normalized-data contract with the exact optional break-glass input shape, accepted object-ID format and sanitization, in-memory/no-commit handling, and explicit not-evaluable behavior when absent. Ensure ISSUE-0004 can consume it without inventing a new contract.
findings.title: The required break-glass input contract is missing
findings.verification: Review the updated contract against project/issues/ISSUE-0003.md lines 38–52 and confirm tests or subsequent issue acceptance criteria cover supplied, absent, and invalid input.

evidence: Expected: acceptance criterion 2 says multi-page responses are fully followed; failure to complete paging should be reported as an error, not returned as a successful complete result.
Observed: after more than 1000 pages, the client silently breaks and returns the accumulated partial policy list even when a next link remains.
A repeated/cyclic next link likewise causes up to 1001 requests and then a misleading successful partial response.
The current paging test covers only a normal two-page response.
findings.remediation: Track visited URLs and raise a stable GraphError for cycles or when a documented page limit is exceeded; never return a partial collection as a successful complete fetch. Add cycle and limit tests.
findings.title: Paging limit silently returns incomplete policies as success
findings.verification: Test a repeated next link and a sequence exceeding the configured limit; each must raise the documented error and /api/policies must return a structured failure rather than HTTP 200 with partial data.

evidence: Expected: the active issue record should durably identify one starting SHA and the exact candidate under review.

Observed: the record contains two contradictory Starting SHA fields, one exact and one placeholder, and still says Candidate SHA: Not created even though status is REVIEWING and the launcher supplied target 2495c32df08ee11a563122bde4a5fca6fe93fae1.
The repository rules require current records to identify the reviewed candidate without relying on chat or launcher-only context.
findings.remediation: Remove the duplicate placeholder and bind Candidate SHA to 2495c32df08ee11a563122bde4a5fca6fe93fae1 for this review round. Keep subsequent repair candidates and reports explicitly SHA-bound.
findings.title: Issue metadata does not identify the reviewed candidate consistently
findings.verification: Run the governance validator and inspect the issue/status/handoff records to confirm one base SHA and one exact candidate SHA agree with the next review invocation.

limitations: The full test suite could not complete successfully in this read-only, network-restricted review environment because server tests require a loopback socket.
Compilation could not be independently verified because py_compile requires filesystem writes for bytecode output.
Governance validation could not complete because its smoke tests require a writable temporary directory.
Author-reported successful checks are claims supported only by the committed handoff; raw immutable command output bound to the target commit is not present.
The protected live Graph integration was not exercised, so real tenant consent behavior, response compatibility, and paging remain unverified.
Because mandatory independent execution evidence is unavailable, repository rules require BLOCKED even apart from the substantive findings.
review.summary: BLOCKED: target identity is correct, but independent compile, full tests, and governance validation could not pass in the review sandbox. Static review also found a high-severity bearer-token exfiltration path through unvalidated next links, an incomplete prerequisite data contract, silent partial paging success, and stale candidate metadata.
